title: Hall Rush Pad Thai
seoTitle: Hall Rush Pad Thai | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Sweet-salty noodles, fast wok
description: Sweet-salty noodles, fast wok. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

ingredients.name: Pad Thai sauce (tamarind, fish sauce, sugar)

steps.title: Soak rice noodles
steps.instruction: Soak rice noodles in hot water 20 minutes until pliable; drain.

steps.title: Sear shrimp and scramble eggs
steps.instruction: Sear shrimp in hot oil until pink; push aside. Scramble eggs in the same wok; break into pieces.

steps.title: Toss noodles and sauce
steps.instruction: Add noodles and pad Thai sauce; toss over high heat 2–3 minutes until noodles absorb sauce and char slightly.

steps.title: Finish with crunch
steps.instruction: Fold in bean sprouts and peanuts off heat. Serve with lime wedges. Pad Thai should be tangy, salty, and a little sweet — not oily.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Hall Rush Pad Thai with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Hall Rush Pad Thai on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sweet-salty noodles, fast wok. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
